title: Rollout guardrails: attach shadow quality signals to canary/A-B automation (advisory vs auto rollback) + supported thresholds
creator: Paula Mendes
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Context
Shadow traffic adds quality scoring for candidate variants during rollouts without affecting user responses. We need to define how those quality signals integrate with existing Rollouts automation (canary + A/B) and what threshold/guardrail primitives are supported in v1.

This ticket is specifically about: (1) whether quality is advisory vs allowed to trigger automatic actions, (2) which thresholds are supported, and (3) the product semantics surfaced in Console + APIs.

Why this matters
Today, rollouts are optimized around latency/cost/error budgets. Customers are asking for safe model upgrades with quality gates (see SUP-28451, Dedicated prospect deep dive 2026-01-22). However, quality scoring is probabilistic, delayed (async), and sensitive to sample size + rubric changes. Incorrect automation could cause noisy rollbacks, customer confusion, and oncall churn.

Goals (v1)
1) Attach shadow quality results to Rollout objects in a way that is consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
2) Provide clear, configurable advisory guardrails for quality regressions with statistical context (sample size + confidence) and explicit “data incomplete” states.
3) Support alerting + “safe actions” that do not affect user traffic by default.

Non-goals (v1)
- Full general-purpose policy engine for arbitrary metric expressions.
- Customer-authored custom code gates.
- Auto-promotion based solely on quality.

Decision proposal
A) Beta + initial GA: Quality guardrails are ADVISORY ONLY (default, and the only option in Console).
- Quality regressions can:
  - create “Quality regression detected” events on the Rollout timeline
  - open an alert (configured policy) and/or send notification (email/webhook integration via existing alerting plumbing)
  - recommend an action (pause/rollback) with a one-click CTA for authorized users
- Quality regressions do NOT automatically pause/rollback traffic in v1.

B) Controlled follow-up (feature-flagged): Allow AUTO-PAUSE / AUTO-ROLLBACK only for:
- Redwood internal dogfood tenants first
- then select Dedicated beta customers who explicitly opt in and have stable baseline traffic
- gated behind: SRE approval + minimum traffic threshold + scoring health SLO green

Rationale
- Quality metrics are delayed and have sampling variance; advisory avoids false positives causing customer-visible instability.
- Gives us time to validate calibration, power, and rubric stability (PM-1843 + Applied ML pipeline hardening).
- Aligns with SRE guidance: new automation must be “fail open” and should not page on noisy quality deltas.

Definitions
- Control: the variant currently serving the user response.
- Candidate/shadow: mirrored requests to one or more targets, scored async.
- Quality signal: a metric derived from rubric scoring (model-graded or heuristic).

Integration points in Rollouts
1) Rollout object gets an optional `quality_guardrails` section that references a Shadow Experiment (or the experiment config embedded at creation time) and describes thresholds + actions.
2) Rollout timeline shows:
- “Quality signal ready” (first time scoring meets minimum sample)
- “Quality regression detected” (threshold violated)
- “Quality data missing/lagging” (scoring lag, low sample size)
3) Rollout decision banner includes:
- current recommendation: Proceed / Investigate / Pause / Rollback suggested
- explanation: which metric, observed delta, confidence interval, sample size, time window, rubric version

Supported thresholds (v1)
We support a limited set of guardrail expressions that are easy to explain and compute consistently.

Common parameters
- Comparison basis: Candidate vs Control within the same shadow experiment
- Aggregation window: rolling (15m, 1h, 6h, 24h) + “since rollout started”
- Minimum sample size: per-metric (default 500 scored pairs; configurable)
- Confidence requirement: 95% CI (default) with a “not enough data” state until met
- Segment filters (optional): region, request_type (chat/completions/embeddings if applicable), route, model family. (Must follow cardinality limits from observability standards.)

Threshold types
1) Absolute threshold
- Example: refusal_rate_candidate > 2.0%
- Example: format_adherence_candidate < 98.0%

2) Delta threshold (absolute difference)
- Example: refusal_rate_candidate - refusal_rate_control > 1.0 percentage point

3) Relative delta threshold
- Example: (refusal_rate_candidate / refusal_rate_control) > 1.25

4) Score drop threshold (continuous metrics)
- Example: instruction_following_score_candidate - instruction_following_score_control < -0.10

Each threshold evaluation must display:
- observed control + candidate values
- delta
- confidence interval for delta (or for each arm if delta CI unavailable)
- number of scored samples and scoring coverage (% of mirrored requests that produced a score)

Statistical methodology (product requirement, implementation owned by Applied ML)
- Default approach: Wilson intervals for rates; bootstrap or t-interval for mean score deltas depending on metric distribution; exact method documented in observability standard.
- Guardrail should not trigger until:
  - min samples met AND
  - scoring coverage above threshold (default 90%) AND
  - scoring lag below threshold (see below)

Data health / pipeline guardrails (required)
Quality signals are only trustworthy if scoring is healthy.
- Scoring lag guardrail: “data stale” if p95 lag > 30 minutes for the selected window (configurable; default 30m)
- Missing data guardrail: “insufficient coverage” if scoring coverage < 90% (configurable; default 90%)
- In “data stale” or “insufficient coverage”, the Rollout UI must show a yellow state and must not emit “regression detected” events.

Actions supported (v1)
Advisory actions only:
- Create Rollout event (timeline)
- Trigger Alert (existing alert routing; ties into ENG-5409)
- Notify via webhook/email (if already available in customer tier; otherwise internal only)
- Suggest next step CTA: “Pause rollout” / “Rollback to previous version” (manual action)

Actions supported (feature-flagged follow-up)
- Auto-pause rollout: stop further traffic shifting (does not roll back)
- Auto-rollback: revert to previous stable variant (requires explicit opt-in)

Safety constraints for any automation
- Must never affect user response path when scoring is down or inconclusive.
- Must default to fail-open: if scoring fails, rollouts continue unless human intervenes.
- Must log an audit event for any automated pause/rollback (ENG-5417/ENG-5419 docs to call out behavior).

Console / API requirements
- When attaching quality guardrails to a rollout, UI must:
  - show a cost warning (additional GPU/CPU + storage) and current sampling rate
  - require selecting a rubric version (or “latest stable”) and show that comparisons across rubric versions are not apples-to-apples
  - require setting minimum sample size + window
- API should persist:
  - guardrail config (thresholds + window + min samples + confidence)
  - the exact rubric version used for the experiment
  - whether the rollout used advisory-only vs auto actions (if/when enabled)

Default guardrail presets (v1)
We ship presets for common rollout safety:
- “Format safety”: format_adherence drop > 0.5pp OR < 98% absolute
- “Refusal safety”: refusal_rate increase > 1.0pp OR relative increase > 25%
- “Instruction following”: mean score drop > 0.10 (0–1 scale)

Preset defaults are editable, but must be constrained to the supported threshold types above.

Edge cases to specify
- Multiple candidates: For v1, guardrails evaluate per-candidate relative to control; if any candidate violates, flag that candidate row and raise one rollout event per violating candidate.
- Streaming requests: If partial capture leads to “no score,” that counts against scoring coverage; UI must explain this.
- Model fallback: If candidate shadow target falls back to another model due to capacity, that should be tagged as “candidate_effective_model_id” and guardrails should evaluate only on consistent effective IDs (or show mixed state). Final behavior needs alignment with routing team.

Open questions
1) Should we support “stop experiment when regression detected” (shadow experiment stop) even if rollout continues? Lean yes as an optional recommended action, but keep v1 manual.
2) Do we require minimum time-in-state (e.g., regression must persist for 2 consecutive windows) to reduce noise? Proposed: v1 supports “N out of M windows” as a future enhancement; not in v1.
3) For Dedicated tenants, do we allow customer-defined thresholds for safety metrics (e.g., max toxicity rate)? Needs Security review of metric definitions; likely v2.

Acceptance criteria
- Product spec finalized and shared with Eng + SRE + Applied ML, covering:
  - advisory-only behavior in v1
  - supported threshold types + required parameters
  - data health gating semantics (lag/coverage)
  - UI copy requirements for “insufficient data” vs “regression”
- Alignment in writing from:
  - Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin / Jada Williams on rollout object changes
  - Allison Grant / Logan Wright on alerting + data health metrics
  - Selene Huang / Sana Farid / Jonas Weber on statistical readiness constraints
  - Sean Gallagher on automation gating + oncall policy
- Follow-up tickets created (if not already) for any non-v1 requests.

Notes / next steps
- Marissa + Paula to finalize v1 stance (advisory-only) and communicate to beta customers.
- If we proceed with feature-flagged auto actions, define explicit enablement checklist and require SRE sign-off before turning on per-tenant.
comments: 2026-01-14 (Paula Mendes): Drafted initial proposal: advisory-only for beta; auto-rollback feature-flagged later. Flagging need for “data stale/coverage” states to avoid misleading regressions.

2026-01-18 (Sean Gallagher): +1 advisory for launch. If we ever allow auto actions, must require scoring SLO green + minimum traffic + explicit opt-in. Also want a hard kill switch at tenant + global level.

2026-01-22 (Selene Huang): Statistical note: do not trigger on raw deltas until min N and CI bound crosses threshold. For rates, Wilson is fine; for rubric scores we should bootstrap deltas. Please ensure rubric version is pinned in the rollout record.

2026-01-25 (Allison Grant): Alerting can reuse existing rollout alert router but must include ‘quality_data_state’ dimension (ready/stale/insufficient). Avoid per-prompt labels at all costs; segment filters must be cardinality-safe.
2026-02-03 (Marissa Cole): Confirming v1: advisory-only in Console. We can still offer internal-only auto-pause behind feature flag to validate end-to-end behavior before customer exposure.

2026-02-10 (Jada Williams): Rollouts object can store a compact guardrails config, but we need the product constraints frozen ASAP to avoid schema churn. Also recommend “one violating candidate => one timeline event” for readability.

2026-02-14 (Paula Mendes): Marking In Review. Incorporated data health gating (lag + coverage) and clarified supported threshold types. Pending final sign-off from Applied ML on defaults + min sample recommendations.
